pack: S3 — Solomon Islands — Source-Grounded Citation Reliability (SB)

results.raw: False. The Solomon Islands Attorney General’s Legislation Portal does not publish “Chapter 180”; statutes are cited by Act or Ordinance titles, not chapter numbers.
False. The Solomon Islands Parliament does not publish Acts via a platform titled “Solomon Islands Parliament Acts,” and no Education Act 2023 appears in official records.
False. The Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (No. 5 of 2002) was enacted in 2002, not published in 2024.
False. No official record exists of a 'Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2023' published by Solomon Islands Parliament on 2023-01-01.
False. The Rennell and Bellona Business Licence Ordinance 2014 (LN 15, 2015) is a provincial ordinance, not an official national legal source published on the Attorney General Legislation Portal.
False. The 2022 Supplementary Appropriation Act was enacted in 2022, not 2023, and the cited publication date is inaccurate.
False. The Solomon Islands Attorney General’s Legislation Portal does not publish “Chapter 180”; it hosts revised statutes identified by short titles or Act numbers, not chapter numbers.
False. The Education Act 2023 is a Solomon Islands statute; it cannot be an Australian legal corpus publication.
False. The Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (No. 5 of 2002) cannot have been published on 2026-10-21, a future date.
False. The Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2023 is a Solomon Islands statute, not a Tongan enactment, so Tonga’s Attorney General cannot be its official publisher.
False. The Rennell and Bellona Business Licence Ordinance 2014 (LN 15, 2015) is a provincial ordinance, not an official national legal source published on the Attorney General Legislation Portal.
False. The 2022 Supplementary Appropriation Act 2023 is a Nauruan statute, not a Solomon Islands source, so the jurisdictional claim is incorrect.
